metadata.title: What Do We Know about Young People’s Interest in Health Careers? (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document synthesizes evidence from PISA survey data and from national administrative programme data on nursing education admissions; it does not provide an analytic student-level estimation workflow with a clearly defined final analytic sample for a single ML model. Because it is a review of existing data sources rather than an original micro-data analysis, complex survey weighting variables (e.g., PISA student weights) are not specified for a unified estimation procedure. For any secondary analyses using PISA microdata, analysts should apply the PISA sampling weights and follow the PISA technical documentation for variance estimation under the complex survey design. Plausible values (if used for cognitive outcomes) should be handled according to the PISA scaling approach, but this review does not report a single PV/weighting implementation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a review that summarizes findings from PISA and administrative nursing education data rather than estimating a single student-level model with a specified PV-based cognitive outcome. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the review’s reported synthesis, and the paper does not document a missing-data strategy for an original analytic dataset. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported because there is no single empirical modeling pipeline whose imputation/deletion rules can be evaluated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 responses from the set of participating countries and economies mentioned in the annex (80 participating countries and economies) and combined these with national administrative programme data on nursing education admissions; the review does not specify a single analytic subsample definition for an original student-level estimation dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD review synthesizes evidence on young people’s interest in health careers using PISA survey data on career aspirations of 15-year-old students and complements it with national administrative data on applications and admissions to nursing education programmes. The review organizes results around students’ aspirations to work in the health sector, aspirations to work as doctors, and aspirations to work as nurses, with additional attention to gender differences. It also reports evidence from an online search of data sources for a subgroup of OECD countries and discusses how administrative data are reported across OECD and non-OECD contexts. Because the document is a synthesis rather than a single empirical ML study, it does not report model-based performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) or a unified predictive pipeline. Consequently, the implications are primarily descriptive and policy-oriented, highlighting where gendered patterns and data availability constraints may affect workforce planning and outreach strategies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided article text contains only section headings and a high-level description of data sources (PISA 2022 and administrative nursing admissions data) without reporting an original empirical modeling procedure, sample sizes, country-level Ns, or ML algorithms/metrics. As a result, fields such as total_students, countries with per-country sample sizes, and any PV/missing-data handling for a specific analytic dataset cannot be populated from the excerpt. The document should be treated as a review/synthesis of evidence rather than an ML prediction paper with a single estimand and reported performance.
